VisualLanguageProfile.description: How the reference builds its scenes. Every field is optional; omit or null what is unclear.

asset_character.description: The dominant kind of visual material.

description:
Reusable style principles observed in a reference video. Every dimension is optional:
omit it, or give `"value": null`, when the reference does not show it clearly. Values are
tendencies of the whole piece, never instructions for a particular frame.

approximate_palette_evidence.description:
Up to 8 approximate colors copied from the deterministic evidence (`color.palette`).
Evidence only: the engine maps them into its own curated palette families.

background_character.description: What typically sits behind the content.

composition_rhythm.description: How often the composition meaningfully changes (from visual change, never audio).

contrast.description: Tonal contrast between grounds and content.

image_treatment.description: How photographs or illustrations are treated. `none` when the reference has no images.

layer_activity.description: How present/active the foreground, midground and background layers are.

material_character.description: Surface finish of grounds and graphic elements.

polarity.description: Light or dark design. `mixed` when both are substantial.

reference_fingerprint.description:
The `reference_fingerprint` of the analysis bundle this profile was written from
(copy it from the request). Optional, but required for provenance checks.

scale_contrast.description: Size contrast between the dominant element and supporting elements.

temperature.description: Color temperature of grounds and dominant colors.

transition_character.description: How one composition hands off to the next.

typography_contrast.description: How strongly type sizes/weights/styles contrast with each other.

unsupported_reference_traits.description: Visible traits the engine cannot render. Recorded, never imitated.

visual_density.description: How much visual information a typical frame holds around its main focus.

visual_language.description:
(v0.2) How the reference constructs its scenes: medium, imagery use, composition families,
visual explanation. Patterns only, never copied scenes.
